USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Use the Osaka G20 meeting to restart talks without firing the threatened List 4 tariffs on the remaining ~$300B of Chinese consumer goods, and without rolling back existing Section 301 tariffs or the Huawei Entity List. Condition any pause in further escalation on China returning to the pre-May draft (purchases plus enforceable IP, tech-transfer, and SOE language). Keep List 4 and export-control pressure as reserved leverage rather than using them on the eve of a leader meeting.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is moderately elevated, not existential and not a clean opportunity. After the May 5 breakdown and the May 10 List 3 hike to 25%, China raised duties on its ~$60B U.S. list (effective June 1), halted further soybean goodwill buying, and signaled rare-earth and "unreliable entity" counters after the May 16 Huawei Entity List. That bites a core U.S. export constituency: USDA authorized up to $16B in farm aid, soybean exports to China had already collapsed (~75% drop in 2018 value; Jan–Oct 2018 shipments down 63% y/y), and NY Fed work put the existing tariff stack at about $831 per household—costs that would jump if List 4 (phones, computers, clothing) proceeds. Markets are pricing slower growth: the 10-year yield fell from 2.69% (end-2018) to 2.05% on June 26, the 2-year to 1.77%, and the 3-month/10-year curve inverted, prompting Powell to say the Fed is "closely monitoring" trade and will "act as appropriate." That is real but still short of a +0.5 national GDP-drag reading: the expansion is intact, China’s own April IP (+5.4%) and retail sales (+7.2%) slowed, and Washington still holds unused List 4 leverage. Action should therefore be negotiate, not escalate or concede. Mnuchin said the sides were ~90% toward a text before Beijing walked back commitments and that the U.S. will re-engage if China returns to that text; a senior official said Washington will not arrive with concessions and that imposing the remaining tariffs would likely kill talks. A Buenos Aires-style pause-and-talk is the available off-ramp; a unilateral rollback would reward the May reneging, while List 4 now would hit U.S. consumers, invite full Chinese retaliation (remaining U.S. goods, rare earths, U.S. firms in China), and close the window the June 18 Trump–Xi call just opened.
key_factors: Osaka G20 Trump-Xi meeting is the first leader contact since the May collapse; best feasible outcome is a tariff truce plus resumed talks, not a signed deal
Existing $250B at 25% plus Huawei Entity List already impose costs; List 4 would shift the burden onto U.S. consumer goods and likely end negotiations
Farm-belt retaliation is the clearest U.S. vulnerability (soy halt, $16B USDA aid) and would worsen if escalation continues
Bond market and Fed reaction (10-year at 2.05%, curve inversion, Powell insurance language) show trade risk is now a macro, not just sectoral, constraint
U.S. still has unused leverage and China’s data have softened, so conceding the May text or rolling back tariffs now would give away position without a matching offer

CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Use the Osaka G20 meeting to reopen talks without new structural, legal, or purchase commitments. The near-term aim is to freeze the pending ~$300B U.S. consumer-goods tariff list and test whether a limited Huawei licensing path can be discussed without surrendering the May red lines (extra-tariff removal, realistic purchase volumes, a balanced text). Do not populate the unreliable-entity list or restrict rare-earth exports before the meeting; keep those as reserve leverage. Hold the June 1 retaliation already in force rather than adding a new strike that might trigger the remaining U.S. list.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high, not existential. After May 10, List 3 sits at 25% on ~$200B and combined Section 301 coverage is ~$250B; Washington is mid-hearing on tariffs covering essentially all remaining Chinese exports (~$300B, including phones, computers, clothing). The May 16 Entity List plus Google/chip cutoffs hit Huawei—China’s 5G and smartphone champion—harder than tariffs alone; the 90-day Temporary General License only covers existing networks/handsets through 19 August and leaves the listing in place. That matches the CHN +0.5 anchor (export sectors, firm-level targeting, unemployment risk) but not +1.0: services PMI held at 54.3, official urban jobless was still 5% in May, reserves remain large, and a leaders’ meeting is already set. The real-economy bite is visible: official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.4 in May with new export orders at 46.5 and the employment sub-index at 47.0 (weakest since March 2009); May industrial output grew only 5.0% y/y, a 17-year low; the yuan is approaching the psychologically important 7 per dollar. U.S. 10-year yields dropped to ~2.05% by 26 June, consistent with a global growth scare. Action should stay near zero because further Chinese escalation (rare-earth embargo, full unreliable-entity implementation) the day before Osaka would raise the odds the U.S. proceeds with the $300B list and hardens the Huawei cutoff, while unilateral purchase or legal concessions would ratify the May collapse on Washington’s terms—U.S. officials said on 26 June they will not accept conditions on tariff use and expect no deal at the summit, only a path back to talks. Liu He already stated the three conditions after the May breakdown; those remain the right bargaining position. Explore de-escalation; do not pre-pay for it.
key_factors: List 3 now 25% on ~$200B; ~$300B remaining list in USTR hearings and explicitly threatened if Osaka fails
Huawei Entity List plus Android/chip cutoff is a tech-sovereignty shock; TGL is narrow and expires 19 August
May PMI 49.4, export orders 46.5, IP growth 5.0% (17-year low) show the dispute is already hitting factories and jobs
G20 Osaka meeting is set (phone call 18 June); U.S. goal is to reopen talks, not sign a deal
China already retaliated on ~$60B and signaled rare earths / unreliable-entity list — further escalation now has poor second-order payoff
Liu He red lines (tariff removal, realistic purchases, balanced text) remain unmet; concede_purchases is premature
